This page is the specification of cadjoint's interface: how it looks and how it
behaves. It is written as a short list of axioms followed by everything derived
from them. A rule below that cannot be traced to an axiom is a bug in this page;
a screen that contradicts a rule is a bug in the screen.

The measurements behind the choices (contrast ratios, ramp distances, the glass
and motion-blur studies) are in [the design-language research
note](../research/design-language.md). This page states the result; that note
argues for it.

## Axioms

**A1 — The part and its numbers are the subject.** The interface is the sheet
they are printed on. Nothing in the chrome may be more salient than the geometry
or a measured value.

**A2 — The program is the truth.** Every edit made anywhere in the interface is
an edit to the source text, and the screen is a rendering of that text. There is
no state the program does not hold, apart from the view (camera, layout,
selection).

**A3 — Hue is meaning.** Every hue on screen belongs to exactly one role in a
closed table ([Colour roles](#colour-roles)). Anything without a role is drawn
without hue: ink on paper.

**A4 — Never by hue alone.** Every role also has a carrier that survives
greyscale and colour-blindness: a word, a shape, a position or a weight.

**A5 — Contrast is a number.** Text clears 4.5:1 against its ground. A mark
that carries meaning clears 3:1. Furniture (grids, resting hairlines) sits in a
band below that, so it is visible without competing.

**A6 — One unit.** Every length is a multiple of the unit `u = 4px`. Half a unit
(2px) is allowed inside a control. The one sub-unit length is the hairline, 1px.

**A7 — Structure is drawn, not stacked.** Things are separated by rules and
grouped by shared edges. There is no shadow, no radius and no translucency
behind text.

**A8 — Two voices.** What the program says (names, values, units, labels of the
instrument) is set in mono. What a person says (sentences) is set in sans.

**A9 — Motion shows causality.** Something moves only to show that one thing
happened because of another. Anything else is still.

**A10 — Every action answers.** An action is acknowledged within 100 ms, says
what it is doing while it runs, and ends in a visible state: done, failed (with
the reason), or cancelled.

**A11 — Every step can be taken back.** An edit is undoable, a gesture is
abandonable, a mode is escapable, one step at a time.

A1–A9 govern appearance, A2, A10 and A11 govern behaviour. They are ordered: when
two rules conflict, the one derived from the earlier axiom wins.

## Colour

### The ground and the ink

From A1 and A7: the ground is paper, and the chrome and the viewport share it.
The seam between them is a rule, not a step in brightness.

| token | value | on paper | job |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ground` | `#e6e6e9` | — | the page and the viewport |
| `ground-step` | `#edecee` | 1.06:1 | sub-bars; hover (a step *down* from `sheet`) |
| `sheet` | `#f8f7f8` | 1.17:1 | panels, popovers, dialogs |
| `ink` | `#18161a` | 14.4:1 | primary text, selection |
| `ink-2` | `#48464d` | 7.5:1 | secondary text, icons, hover |
| `ink-3` | `#605e65` | 5.1:1 | labels, units, construction geometry |
| `rule` | `#9f9da5` | 2.2:1 | hairlines inside a panel (furniture) |
| `rule-strong` | `#747278` | 3.8:1 | control edges, section breaks, the viewport seam |
| `rule-heavy` | `#36343b` | 9.9:1 | the viewport frame, the active indicator |

There are three ink levels and no fourth. Text is never faded with `opacity`,
because a faded text has no contrast ratio that can be asserted (A5). A
disabled control uses `ink-3` and loses its edge, and it does not fade.

There are two sheets above the ground, and no third. A proposed surface less than
3 ΔOKLab from an existing one is that surface.

### Colour roles

From A3. This table is closed: a new hue needs a new row here first.

| role | token | value | means | carrier (A4) | zone |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **current** | `accent` | `#f87318` | the thing you are acting on or in: the active mode, the selected row, the primary action, the source span being edited | a filled block; position | chrome |
| **free** | `param` | `#0065b4` | a free parameter: a value the optimiser or a drag may move, through which gradients flow | the word *free*; a count | chrome, editor |
| **error** | `danger` | `#a8341c` | failed, violated, destructive | the word; ✕ / filled square | chrome, editor |
| **warning** | `warn` | `#8a5a00` | stale, approximate, needs attention | the word; triangle | chrome, editor |
| **done** | `ok` | `#00734c` | converged, satisfied, connected | the word; ● | chrome |
| **direction** | `axis-x/y/z` | `#c81e2a` `#17742a` `#1f5fd2` | world X, Y, Z | the letter | viewport, view cube |
| **field** | viridis | ramp | a solved nodal field (temperature, displacement, stress) | legend with labelled ends | viewport, legend |
| **quality** | magma | ramp | mesh quality | legend with labelled ends | viewport, legend |
| **distance** | `sdf-inside/outside` | `#6400fd` / `#8a5601` | signed distance, inside / outside | zero isoline; legend | viewport, legend |
| **boundary** | `bc-*` | nine hues | the boundary condition of each kind | swatch beside its name | viewport, BC list |
| **proposal** | `proposal` | `#1b7987` | the builder's live selection preview | appears only while building | viewport |

Everything else is achromatic, and that includes four things that are often
coloured elsewhere:

- **Selection** is `ink`, the heaviest tone, so it reads over any field value.
- **Hover** is `ink-2`.
- **Constraints** are `ink`. A constraint holds geometry still, and in this
  table stillness has no hue. A *violated* constraint is `danger`.
- **Construction geometry** (sketch edges, planes, mesh wire) is `ink-3`,
  `rule` when locked.

**The accent is a fill, never ink.** As a ground under `ink-on-accent`
(`#0a0a0c`) it measures 7.0:1; as text or a hairline on paper it measures 2.3:1.
The first passes and the second fails, so the accent appears only as a block
with near-black type on it. `accent-press` (`#c85d00`, 3.4:1) is the pressed
fill and the only accent-coloured mark. Because the accent means *current*, at
most a few accent blocks are on screen at once: the mode, the primary action of
the focused panel, and the selection.

**A label of kind is inverse ink, not accent.** Section kickers (`LIBRARY`,
`FEM`, `READ-ONLY`) and kind chips (`THERMAL`, `ELASTIC`) are `sheet` type on an
`ink` block. They say what something *is*, and *current* is the accent's one
meaning.

### Zones

1. **Chrome hue stays outside the viewport rectangle.** Inside it the only hues
   are the data roles (field, quality, distance, boundary, proposal) and
   direction.
2. **A role may share a hue family with another only across zones.** `ok` and
   `axis-y` are both green; one is a status in a panel and the other a direction
   in the viewport, and they never label the same thing. The traction BC and
   `axis-x` are both red, and they never share a mode, because BCs show in
   Simulate and the gizmo shows in Model and Sketch.
3. **A ramp appears in a panel only as a legend**: a bar at most 8px tall with
   both ends labelled in units. A ramp without numbers is decoration.
4. **Nothing marks a reading by recolouring it.** Hover and selection over a
   field are drawn as an outline; the field pixels keep their true value.
5. **No text sits on a backdrop that depends on the data.** A surface carrying
   glyphs or a legend is opaque.

### The editor

From A3: syntax highlighting is not a role, so it is achromatic. Keywords are
`ink` semibold, names `ink`, strings `ink-2`, comments `ink-3` italic,
punctuation `ink-2`. The editor's hues are its roles: `danger` and `warn` for
diagnostics, `param` for the gutter mark on lines that carry a free parameter,
and the accent for the span the viewport selection points at.

## Type

From A8. Mono is the house face: labels, tabs, menus, values, units, names from
the program. Sans is for sentences: hints, help, warnings, dialog text, and the
prose of these docs.

| token | px | job |
|---|---|---|
| `text-3xs` | 9 | tracked uppercase labels and kickers |
| `text-2xs` | 10 | dense secondary text, selector expressions |
| `text-xs` | 11 | control labels, tabs, menu items, hints |
| `text-sm` | 12 | body; the default |
| `text-md` | 13 | values the user reads |
| `text-lg` | 15 | panel titles, and nothing else |

The scale is steps of 1px between 9 and 13, where each step is about 10 % of the
size (just above the visible threshold), and then one jump to the single title
size. Weights are 400, 500 and 600; 700 only on an accent block.

**Tracking is a function of size**: 0.16em at 9px, falling to 0.04em at 15px.
Uppercase is for furniture only. A string that came from the program (`fin
comb`, `sink-conduction`) is quoted as written: never uppercased, never
restyled.

**Numbers** are tabular, right-aligned on a shared column, and one size above
their label. The unit follows the value in `ink-3`, one size smaller, on the
same baseline, and disappears with the value. Decimal places are the tolerance,
so precision is chosen per quantity and never padded.

## Space and size

From A6, every length is a multiple of 4px.

**Spacing.** `2 · 4 · 6 · 8 · 12 · 16 · 24` (½ to 6 units). The two half-unit
steps live inside controls. Padding inside a panel is at least 8px; when a panel
runs out of room, density comes from type (a 9px label over a 13px value) and
not from smaller gaps.

**Control heights.** `20 · 24 · 28 · 32 · 36`, five to nine units.

| token | px | job |
|---|---|---|
| `control-tag` | 20 | non-interactive tags and chips |
| `control-sm` | 24 | the smallest thing you can click: dense rows, inline buttons |
| `control-md` | 28 | inputs, selects, buttons in panels |
| `control-lg` | 32 | the toolbar, tool-rail cells |
| `control-xl` | 36 | the top bar |

24px is the floor for anything interactive because it is the minimum target
size in WCAG 2.2 (2.5.8). Every control in a row picks the same height, so
labels, inputs and icons share a baseline.

**Lines.** `hairline` is 1px and is the only border weight. `stroke-active` is
2px and means one thing: *this is the active one* (the active tab, the focused
input's edge). A 2px line used for emphasis is wrong.

## Shape and elevation

From A7.

- **Radius is zero.** Circles appear only where roundness means *a point, not a
  region*: status dots and vertex handles.
- **No shadow.** Elevation is a lighter sheet plus a `rule-strong` edge. A
  popover is a `sheet` with a hairline, and a modal dialog adds a scrim of `ink`
  at 42 %.
- **Hairlines over boxes.** The default separator is a 1px `rule` that runs the
  full width of the container's padding. A filled box needs a reason, and *it is
  a card* is not one.
- **No inset control.** A field drawn darker than its sheet reads as disabled.
  Inputs are `sheet` with a `rule-strong` edge.
- **Dashed means *not yet*.** A dashed edge marks something that does not exist
  yet: an *add* button, a drop target, a plane label being placed.

## Iconography

- 16px box, 1.25px stroke, no fills, miter joins, square caps, drawn on the
  half pixel so a vertical stroke lands on a device pixel.
- Icons are `ink-2`, and `ink` when active. Icons have no hue (A3): an icon that
  needs a colour needs a word instead.
- Every tool-rail icon has a text label at widths of 1280px and above.
  Destructive actions always carry the word.
- Icons do not appear inside the viewport. Gizmos and handles are geometry,
  drawn by the renderer.

## Motion

From A9. Three durations, named by what they mean.

| token | ms | meaning | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dur-fast` | 90 | acknowledgement: the pointer's own feedback | hover, press |
| `dur-base` | 160 | state: something you directly caused | tab switch, toggle, popover |
| `dur-slow` | 260 | propagation: something changed *because* something else did | the source span lights, then the geometry updates |

One easing family: `ease` (`cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`) for arrivals,
`ease-inout` for things that move and settle.

Causal pairs are sequenced, never simultaneous: when a drag rewrites the source,
the changed span highlights first and the geometry follows. **Never animated**:
digits (a tweened number shows values that were never true), the camera under
direct manipulation, layout on data arrival. Replaying a recorded optimisation
trajectory is not animation, because every frame is a state the optimiser held.
Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, `dur-fast` and `dur-base` become 0 and
propagation becomes a two-frame highlight.

## Components

Every component below is built only from the tokens above.

### Panels

A panel is a dock window: a tab strip (`control-lg`, `ground`), then a `sheet`
body with 8px padding. The body opens with a **header**: an inverse-ink kicker
naming the panel's kind, then the title in `text-lg` tracked mono. Sections
below are separated by a `rule`, each introduced by a 9px tracked label. Panels
are docked, not floated over the viewport, unless the user floats them.

### Rows

A row is `label | … | value` on one baseline at `control-sm` or `control-md`.
The label is `ink-3` 9–11px uppercase; the value is `ink` 13px tabular,
right-aligned. Value columns line up across rows and across panels side by
side. A row that needs a second line hangs a 10px `ink-3` sub-line under the
value.

### Controls

| control | rest | hover | active / pressed | disabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **primary button** (one per panel) | `accent` fill, `ink-on-accent` 700 | — | `accent-press` | `ground-step` fill, `ink-3`, no edge |
| **button** | `sheet`, `rule-strong` edge, `ink-2` | `ground-step` | `ink` edge | `ink-3`, `rule` edge |
| **quiet button** (icon, tab) | no edge, `ink-2` | `ground-step` | `ink`, `stroke-active` underline for tabs | `ink-3` |
| **destructive** | button with the word, `danger` text | `danger` edge | — | — |
| **segmented** (mode switcher) | cells share edges | `ground-step` | the active cell is an `accent` block | — |
| **input** | `sheet`, `rule-strong` edge | — | focus: `stroke-active` `ink` edge | `ink-3`, `rule` edge |
| **invalid input** | `danger` edge, the text kept as typed | | | |

Focus is always visible as a 2px `ink` ring offset 1px, for keyboard focus
(`:focus-visible`).

### Chips and badges

- **Kind chip**: inverse ink, 9px tracked uppercase, `control-tag`.
- **Value chip** (a constraint `distance · P1–P2 = 1.8`, a material name):
  `sheet`, `rule` edge, mono as written, with a × that removes it.
- **Count badge**: tabular figure in `ink` on `ground-step`. The free-parameter
  count is the one badge that takes a hue, `param`.

### Menus, popovers and dialogs

- **Menu**: a `sheet` with a `rule-strong` edge. Items are `control-sm`,
  left-aligned in one column, the shortcut right-aligned in `ink-3`. A check or
  dot sits in a fixed leading column, so labels stay aligned whether or not they
  carry one. The highlighted item is `ground-step`; the open menu's title in the
  bar is the accent block.
- **Popover**: a menu that holds controls. It opens next to its trigger, closes
  on Escape and on a click outside, and never covers its trigger.
- **Dialog**: only for a decision that blocks everything else (an overwrite
  without undo, export settings). It has a scrim, a title, sans prose, and the
  buttons bottom-right with the primary last. Escape is Cancel.

### Notices

There are no transient toasts that disappear on a timer, because a timer decides
when you have read something. Feedback goes in one of three places:

- **in place**, beside the thing it is about (an invalid input, a failed study
  card), and this is the default;
- **the status line**, for the state of the whole program (compiling, compiled,
  out of date);
- **a notice bar** at the top of the viewport for a failure of the whole
  picture (a compile error). It is opaque, `danger` text on `sheet`, names the
  line, and stays until the cause is fixed or it is dismissed.

### Status and work

The toolbar's job chip names the running job that decides whether the screen
matches the code (the compile), and then how many others run. The Processes
window lists them all. A running job states its stage in words (`MESH`,
`SOLVE`) and any quantity that is genuinely known, and has a stop control.
There is no indeterminate spinner over content that is already legible, and no
percentage of an unknown total.

### Viewport overlays

The viewport is an instrument face (A1). Its overlays are achromatic unless they
are data or direction.

| overlay | rest | hover | selected | locked |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sketch edge | `ink-3` | `ink-2` | `ink` | `rule` |
| vertex handle: free | hollow ● `ink-2` | `ink` | filled ● `ink` | — |
| vertex handle: held | filled ■ `ink-3` with lock | `ink-2` | `ink` | `rule` |
| face | — | `ink` outline, 12 % fill | `ink` outline | 45 % outline |
| sketch plane | `ink-3` outline, 8 % fill | `ink-2` | `ink` | `rule` |
| mesh wire / feature edge | `ink-3` 30 % / `ink` | | | |
| gizmo | `axis-x/y/z` arrows and rings | thicker | — | — |

- **Free versus held is shape**: a free vertex is a hollow circle and a held one
  a filled square. In the viewport this replaces the free hue (`param`), which
  stays in the chrome.
- **Dimension and constraint labels** are `ink` mono on an opaque `sheet` tab.
  A violated constraint's label is `danger` and says by how much.
- **The graticule** is furniture held to 1.4–2.8:1 on paper. It rules the world
  plane the camera most nearly faces and states its spacing (`GRID 1.00 m · XY`)
  on a 1-2-5 ladder, prefixed `>` when the view is not to scale.
- **The view cube and axis triad** use the direction tones and the letters.
- **The title block** (bottom right) lists SCENE / STUDY / MESH / SOLVER / REV,
  with `—` where a field is empty.
- **The hint bar** (bottom) names the mode as an inverse-ink block, followed by
  one line of sans saying what the pointer does now.
- **Legends** are opaque, at most 8px tall, with both ends labelled in units.

## Functional rules

### The program is the truth (A2)

- **Every panel is an editor of literals.** Changing a number in a panel, or
  dragging a handle, rewrites that literal in the source. An argument written as
  an expression is shown as written and is read-only; the panel says so instead
  of offering a field that would overwrite it.
- **Selecting reveals the source.** A precise selection (a vertex) scrolls the
  editor to its literal; a whole object scrolls to its declaration. The editor
  does not take focus when it does so.
- **One selection.** Viewport, object tree, properties and editor show the same
  selection. Selecting in any of them selects in all.
- **The screen says whether it matches the code.** While the program is
  compiling, or the picture is older than the text, the status line says so. A
  stale value is marked in place, never silently kept.
- **The newest edit wins.** A new edit supersedes the work of an older one; the
  older answer is discarded even if it arrives later.

### Direct manipulation

- **Preview while dragging, commit on release.** A drag shows its effect live
  and writes the source once, when the pointer comes up. One gesture is one
  undo step.
- **Escape during a gesture abandons it.** The value returns to what it was
  before the pointer went down, in the viewport and in the source.
- **Snapping is visible.** When a drag snaps (to a grid rung, an axis, a
  detent), the snapped-to thing is drawn for as long as the snap holds.

### Modes and tools

- **Modes are a pipeline**: Model → Sketch → Simulate. A mode changes the tool
  set, the panels and the shortcuts wholesale. It is named in the switcher (the
  accent cell) and in the hint bar.
- **One armed tool.** The armed tool is the accent cell in the rail, and the
  hint bar says what clicking will do. Finishing or cancelling a tool returns to
  Select.
- **A grouped tool remembers its last choice**, and shows it on the group.

### Escape and undo (A11)

- **Escape cancels one thing per press**, most specific first: a gesture in
  flight, then a half-finished command, then the armed tool, then the
  selection, then the mode (back to Model). When nothing applies, Escape does
  nothing.
- **Undo is over the source.** `Ctrl/⌘ Z` restores the previous program text;
  inside the editor it is the editor's own history. Each run, patch and gesture
  is one step.
- **Undo replaces confirmation.** A deletion that can be undone is not
  confirmed. Confirmation is only for what undo cannot reach: overwriting a file
  on disk, discarding unsaved work.

### Feedback and long work (A10)

- **Within 100 ms**: the pressed control changes state.
- **After about a second**: the work appears as a job, in the job chip and in
  Processes, with its stage in words and a stop control.
- **A result outlives its panel.** Closing a panel or switching mode does not
  lose a solve; reopening shows it again.
- **Failure is said in the program's language**: what failed, at which line or
  declaration, and what to do next. Raw tracebacks are behind a disclosure, not
  the first thing shown.
- **Empty states name the missing precondition and the action** (*No results
  yet: solve a study or run a study-backed optimisation*). An empty view still
  draws its frame: graticule, title block with `—`, legend with `—` ends.

### Inputs

- **A value commits on Enter or blur**, and only if it is valid. An invalid entry
  keeps its text, marks the field `danger`, and changes nothing.
- **Units are shown, never typed.** The field holds the number; the unit sits
  after it.
- **Numbers keep their written precision.** A panel does not reformat `0.75` as
  `0.7500`.
- **A disabled control says why** in its tooltip. A control that cannot apply in
  the current mode is not shown at all.

### Keyboard

- **Every action is reachable from the keyboard**, and every shortcut appears in
  the Help sheet, which is generated from the same table the handlers use.
- **Single-key shortcuts act only when the viewport has focus.** In a text field
  the keys type.
- **Focus order follows reading order**: menu bar, toolbar, editor, viewport,
  panels left to right, top to bottom.

### Layout

- **Windows dock, tab, float and minimise.** The layout is remembered per mode,
  and *Reset layout* always restores a working default.
- **Nothing is lost by closing a window.** A closed window is reopened from the
  Window menu with its state intact.
- **Space for arriving data is reserved.** A panel does not grow or shift when a
  result arrives; the slot exists, empty, beforehand.

### Language

- Furniture is uppercase tracked mono (`MESH`, `SOLVE`). Program strings are
  verbatim. Sentences are sans, sentence case, without a trailing period when
  they are a single clause.
- Quantities are SI with the unit spelled as a symbol (`1.00 m`, `412.8 K`).
- An empty field is `—`, never `0`, `N/A` or blank.

## The docs site

These docs are set in the same language: paper ground, `ink` text, sans prose,
mono for code, headings, tables of values and navigation; zero radius, no
shadow; links in `ink` with an `accent-press` underline (the accent is never
ink). Code blocks are `sheet` with a `rule` edge, highlighted achromatically.

## Tokens: one source

All of the values on this page live in one file,
`frontend/src/tokens.ts`. The stylesheet's custom properties, the docs theme
and the constants the WebGPU shaders use are generated from it, and
`frontend/test/tokens.test.ts` fails when a generated file is out of date, when
a raw colour or length appears outside the token layer, or when a contrast in
this page stops holding.

## What changes in the current playground

Adopting the rules above changes the following in the current playground.

1. **Viewport overlays become achromatic.** Sketch edges were olive, handles
   red, selected edges brown and planes blue; they become the ink ladder, with
   free and held vertices told apart by shape. The orange hover tint over a
   simulated field becomes an outline.
2. **Kickers and kind chips become inverse ink.** `READ-ONLY`, `SELECTION`,
   `LIBRARY`, `FEM`, `THERMAL` were accent blocks, so the accent was on screen
   six or more times and stopped meaning *current*.
3. **The editor's syntax colours go.** Class names were drawn in error red,
   strings in success green, numbers in warning amber.
4. **`info` becomes `param`.** The blue now means only *free parameter*. The
   constraint-count badge, the solver residual line, the plane label and the
   elastic kind chip, which used it for other things, become achromatic.
5. **One set of axis colours.** The gizmo and the view-cube triad drew
   different reds, greens and blues; both use `axis-x/y/z`, darkened so the
   letters clear 4.5:1.
6. **Control heights move onto the 4px grid** (22/26/30/34 → 24/28/32 and a
   20px tag), and interactive targets are never below 24px.
7. **Accent never draws an outline.** The selected material card's orange
   border (2.3:1) becomes an accent block on its label.
8. **Menus align in one column** with a fixed leading column for checks and
   dots (the mode items were centred).
9. **The docs theme moves off Cosmo** onto these tokens.
10. **Leftover dark-theme values are removed** (white-alpha fills, the lime and
    cyan rgba, the bluish element-edge tone), along with an undefined
    `--type-body-small`.
